name: Vitamin A
short: Excess preformed vitamin A can cause liver damage and other toxicity, and high maternal intakes have been associated with birth defects; children and people with liver disease are most vulnerable.
text: A review of vitamin A toxicity reported that intakes of 25,000 to 50,000 IU a day for several months or more can produce multiple adverse effects, that the lowest toxic intakes occurred in people whose liver function was compromised by drugs, viral hepatitis or malnutrition, and that children and pregnant women are especially vulnerable, with birth defects associated with maternal intakes as low as approximately 25,000 IU a day, although a threshold dose for birth defects could not be identified; beta-carotene was much less toxic. A hepatology review describes acute toxicity from high single doses and chronic toxicity from prolonged overconsumption, with nausea, bone pain and liver damage that can progress from fatty liver to fibrosis and cirrhosis. In a meta-analysis of 13 observational studies, high dietary intake of total vitamin A or retinol was associated with a higher risk of hip fracture (risk ratios 1.29 and 1.23), whereas total fracture risk was not associated with any vitamin A compound. The toxicity review noted that certain drugs may markedly potentiate vitamin A toxicity in animals, but no specific medicine interactions were named in the cited sources.
